newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Kinkel rules out postponement EMU - press interview.
newsitem.headline: Kinkel rules out postponement EMU - press interview.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel, in an interview with Portuguese newspaper Publico, ruled out a postponement of the launch of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU).
"A flexible approach to the calendar and the EMU convergence criteria are out of the question," Kinkel told Publico.
"As expected, we have to adopt a strong and solid common currency on January 1 1999," he added.
"The federal government is making every effort to ensure that Germany complies with the Maastricht criteria in 1997," he said.
I am convinced that we will achieve that goal," he added.
"Neither a flexible approach to the criteria, nor a postponement would represent a solution," the minister said.

He was speaking before visiting Lisbon on Wednesday where he will address the Institute of Strategic Studies on German foreign policy and meet his Portuguese counterpart Jaime Gama to discuss a meeting of NATO foreign ministers in Portugal in May.
